goal: audit https://www.example.com for GDPR consent compliance
summary: We'll create an audit called "example.com — Consent & privacy" against https://www.example.com and attach Consent Categories under Standards. Without one attached, a privacy audit runs but reports nothing — the category is what defines "approved".

steps.say: Audits are created from Data Sources. Open the create menu.

targetFallback.description: the Create button on the Data Sources page
the Web Audit item in the create menu

steps.say: This is where the crawl starts. One URL per line if you want several.
Quick setup has no Standards section, so switch to Advanced Setup — that is where rules, consent categories and alerts are attached.

targetFallback.description: the Standards tab in the audit editor

steps.say: Consent Categories is the second sub-tab. If you do not see it, privacy is not enabled on this account — that is a permissions thing, not something you can fix here.
Find the consent category that matches this site. A category is the list of tags, cookies, geos and domains you have decided are allowed.

targetFallback.description: the search box in the consent categories picker

steps.say: Attach it. This is the step people skip — the audit runs happily without one and then reports no privacy findings at all.

targetFallback.description: the "add all" button in the consent categories picker

steps.say: No category matches https://www.example.com yet? Create one here — you will be asked which tags and cookies are approved.
